2018 Q1.gq: We have raised our outlook for medium- and heavy-duty truck market demand slightly to 1.2 million units from 1.15 million units, representing a 10% decline from 2017.

2019 Q2.gq: For the distribution segment, we now expect revenues to be 1% to 5%, compared to our prior guidance of 2% to 6% with a slight adjustment driven by a stronger dollar, and therefore a higher currency headwind.

2019 Q3.gq: We are increasing our outlook for medium- and heavy-duty truck market demand to 1.23 million units or down 7% compared to our prior guidance of down 10% due to the additional prebuy of natural gas trucks that occurred in the third quarter.

2021 Q3.gq: We've lowered our forecast for industry production of heavy-duty trucks in North America to 228,000 units, up 25% compared to 2020, but below our prior guidance of 264,000 units.

2022 Q2.gq: We expect revenues to increase 3% for the year, down from an increase of 6% in our prior guidance, primarily to a lower outlook in China.

2022 Q3.gq: Based on our current forecast, we are maintaining full year 2022 revenue guidance of up 8% versus last year.
2022 Q3.bq: This is below our previous guidance of approximately 15.5% of sales as a result of the lower than expected market in China in the second half of 2022, and the one-time employee bonus investment made in the third quarter.

2022 Q4.gq: So, let me just reiterate the guidance that we had within the Components business.
2022 Q4.bq: With these exclusions considered, EBITDA was $1.1 billion or 16.1% of sales in Q4, above our guidance of 15.5% and stronger than the $705 million or 12.1% reported a year ago.

2023 Q1.gq: We have raised our forecast for total company revenue in 2023 to be up 15% to 20% compared to our prior guidance of up 12% to 17%.

2023 Q2.gq: Based on our current forecast, we are maintaining full-year 2023 revenue guidance of up 15% to 20% versus last year.

2023 Q3.gq: Based on our current forecast, we are raising full year 2023 revenue guidance to be up 18% to 21% versus last year.

2023 Q4.bq: We delivered solid operational results in the fourth quarter, exceeding our expectations for revenue and delivering EBITDA margins in line with our guidance.

2024 Q1.gq: Given the strength of first quarter results and our improved outlook, we've raised our full year expectations for 2024 after adjusting for the separation of Atmus.

2024 Q2.gq: We are raising our guidance for the global power generation market to be up 15% to 20% compared to our prior guidance of up 10% to 15%, driven by continued increases in the data center and mission-critical markets.

2024 Q3.gq: We now expect 2024 Distribution revenues to be up 8% to 11%, an increase of 2% at the midpoint from our prior guidance, primarily due to stronger power generation markets.

2024 Q4.bq: We delivered strong operational results in the fourth quarter, which resulted in revenue achieving the top end of our prior guidance and EBITDA margins exceeding our projections. 2024 was a record year for revenues, EBITDA, and earnings per share, reflecting the strong demand for our products and the strong hard work of our employees.

2026 Q1.gq: We are raising our forecast for total company revenues in 2026 to a range of up 8% to 11% compared to our prior guidance of up 3% to 8%.

2026 Q2.gq: We now expect total company revenues to increase 10% to 13% in 2026 compared to our prior guidance of 8% to 11%.

2026 Q3.gq: For 2026, we now expect revenue growth of 10% to 13% compared with our prior guidance of 9% to 14 and EBITDA margins of 13.6% to 14.1%, a tightening of the prior range of 13.5%.
2026 Q3.bq: Revenues in Q3 were a little below our own expectations.
